lessons.title: Introduction to Next.js
lessons.content:
# Introduction to Next.js

Next.js is a React framework that gives you building blocks to create fast web applications. It handles the tooling and configuration needed for React, and provides additional structure, features, and optimizations for your application.

### Key Features
- **Server-Side Rendering (SSR)**: Render pages on the server for every request.
- **Static Site Generation (SSG)**: Generate HTML at build time.
- **Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)**: Update static content without a full rebuild.
- **File-based Routing**: Routes are defined by the file system structure.

lessons.title: Pages & Routing
lessons.content:
# Pages & Routing

In Next.js, a page is a React Component exported from a file in the `pages` or `app` directory. The path of the file determines the route.

### App Router (Next.js 13+)
- `app/page.tsx` -> `/`
- `app/about/page.tsx` -> `/about`
- `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` -> `/blog/:slug` (Dynamic route)

### Linking between pages
Use the `Link` component for client-side navigation.

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link';

<Link href="/about">About Us</Link>
```

Server vs Client Components
lessons.content:
# Server vs Client Components

### Server Components
- Run on the server.
- No client-side JavaScript (smaller bundle size).
- Great for data fetching and SEO.

### Client Components
- Run on the client.
- Can use Hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`) and Event Listeners.
- Opt-in using the `'use client'` directive at the top of the file.

lessons.title: Image Optimization
lessons.content: # Image Optimization The Next.js Image component (`next/image`) extends the HTML `` element with features for automatic image optimization. ### Benefits - **Size Optimization**: Serve correctly sized images for each device. - **Visual Stability**: Prevent Layout Shift automatically. - **Faster Page Loads**: Images are only loaded when they enter the viewport using native browser lazy loading.

Deployment & SEO
lessons.content:
# Deployment & SEO

Next.js is designed to be deployed to Vercel, the creators of Next.js, for zero-config optimization. It can also be deployed to any hosting provider that supports Node.js or static hosting.

### SEO and Metadata
Next.js has a Metadata API that can be used to define your application metadata (e.g. `meta` and `link` tags inside your HTML `head` element).
